page_title: Double OG Marijuana Strain - Kind Green Buds

source_page_metadata.description: Explore the Double OG marijuana strain - THC levels, genetics, terpene profile, effects, flavor, and grow tips.

article_blocks.text: Strain Type: Indica-dominant hybrid
Genetics: OG Kush backcross
Breeder: California
THC Content: 20–27%
CBD Content: Low (<1%)
Terpene Profile: Myrcene , Limonene , Humulene
Primary Flavors: Earthy, pine, fuel, citrus, herbal
Flowering Time (Indoor): 8–9 weeks
Outdoor Harvest Time: Early to Mid-October
Indoor Yield: 400–500 g/m²
Outdoor Yield: 500–700 g/plant
Grow Difficulty: Moderate

Within the vast family tree of OG genetics, few cultivars embrace the lineage as directly as Double OG . Rather than combining OG Kush with unrelated strains, breeders intensified the defining characteristics of the famous kush line by pairing OG Kush with itself through selective breeding. The result is a marijuana cultivar that amplifies nearly every recognizable trait associated with classic OG varieties —pungent aroma, dense resin production, and a deeply relaxing yet mentally engaging high.

The plant appeals strongly to enthusiasts who appreciate traditional West Coast cannabis profiles. Thick coatings of trichomes, heavy citrus-fuel aromatics, and powerful body effects combine into an experience that feels unmistakably rooted in the OG Kush legacy. For many growers and smokers, this cultivar represents an amplified expression of one of the most influential marijuana genetics ever created.
Genetics and Lineage

The origins of this hybrid trace back to a breeding project by Reservoir Seeds, a seed company recognized for preserving and refining classic cannabis genetics. Instead of introducing outside traits, the breeder stabilized the genetic line by crossing two carefully selected phenotypes of OG Kush. This deliberate pairing sought to reinforce the characteristics that made OG Kush legendary among cannabis connoisseurs.

OG Kush itself occupies a pivotal place in modern marijuana breeding history. Emerging from Southern California during the 1990s, the strain spread rapidly across dispensaries and underground grow operations due to its distinctive terpene profile and powerful psychoactive effects. Over time it became the foundation for countless hybrids, shaping the flavor and potency of contemporary weed varieties.

By doubling down on that genetic foundation, breeders created a cultivar that highlights the strongest attributes of OG Kush. The resulting plants tend to express dense trichome coverage, thick resin production, and an unmistakable kush aroma dominated by pine, fuel, and citrus. Rather than diluting the OG identity, this breeding strategy intensified it, producing a cannabis variety that feels like a concentrated expression of the original lineage.
Effects and Experience

The psychoactive effects typically begin with a noticeable shift in mood and mental atmosphere. Shortly after inhalation, a warm sense of ease spreads through the mind, gently replacing mental tension with a calm, optimistic perspective. The mental component often feels pleasantly euphoric without becoming overly stimulating or chaotic.

As the experience progresses, the physical side of the high gradually becomes more prominent. Muscles begin to loosen, and the body settles into a comfortable state of heaviness. Unlike extremely sedating indica strains that immediately cause couch-lock, this cultivar tends to unfold in stages. The first phase offers mental uplift, while the second phase introduces a deeper wave of bodily relaxation.

Toward the later portion of the experience, the physical calm can become quite pronounced. Many users find themselves naturally slowing down, making the strain well suited for evening use or relaxed social environments. The combination of euphoric mental lift and strong body effects gives the cannabis a balanced character that appeals to fans of classic indica-dominant weed.
Medical Benefits

Medical marijuana patients often gravitate toward kush-based cultivars when seeking relief from physical tension or chronic discomfort. The terpene profile and cannabinoid concentration of this plant may contribute to muscle relaxation and general physical ease. Many individuals exploring cannabis for pain management prefer strains that combine strong THC levels with calming body effects, which this cultivar frequently delivers.

Another area where the plant may prove beneficial involves stress and mental fatigue. The initial euphoric lift can help shift mood away from anxious or racing thoughts, allowing the mind to settle into a calmer rhythm. Because the mental effects remain relatively clear during the early phase of the experience, some patients appreciate its ability to ease stress without immediately inducing heavy sedation.

Sleep support is another reason people explore indica-dominant cannabis genetics. As the experience deepens, the relaxing body sensation may encourage restfulness and help quiet nighttime tension. For individuals struggling to wind down at the end of a long day, strains with strong kush heritage often play a role in evening cannabis routines.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Opening a container of cured flower reveals a strong and unmistakable fragrance dominated by classic OG notes. The aroma typically begins with a sharp citrus brightness reminiscent of lemon peel. Beneath that layer lies the characteristic fuel-like scent associated with kush genetics, giving the overall profile a pungent edge that many cannabis enthusiasts instantly recognize.

Grinding the buds releases deeper aromatic complexity. Earthy pine resin, peppery spice, and faint herbal tones emerge as the trichomes break open. These layered scents come from the interaction of several dominant terpenes —most notably myrcene, limonene, and caryophyllene. Together they create a fragrance that feels both invigorating and grounded.

The flavor closely mirrors the aromatic profile but develops additional nuance during consumption. On the inhale, many people notice bright citrus and pine flavors accompanied by a subtle sweetness. As the smoke or vapor settles on the palate, richer notes of diesel fuel and earthy spice appear. The lingering aftertaste often carries a slightly peppery kush finish that stays noticeable long after exhaling.
Growing Information

Cultivating this marijuana strain generally falls within the moderate difficulty range, making it accessible to growers who already possess some experience with cannabis cultivation . The plants tend to develop a sturdy structure with strong lateral branches capable of supporting dense flower clusters. This architecture allows growers to train the plant effectively and maximize canopy exposure.

Indoor growers typically observe a flowering period between eight and nine weeks. During this stage, the buds become increasingly resinous, often forming thick coatings of trichomes that give the flowers a frosted appearance. Proper air circulation and humidity management are important because the dense structure of kush-style buds can make them susceptible to moisture-related issues if environmental conditions are not carefully controlled.

Outdoor cultivation thrives in climates with warm days and relatively dry autumn weather. Under favorable conditions, plants may reach medium height while producing impressive yields of sticky, aromatic flowers. The harvest window usually falls in early to mid October, depending on regional climate and phenotype variation.
FAQ

Is Double OG a strong marijuana strain? Yes. THC levels often reach the mid-20% range, making the weed quite potent. The combination of high THC and kush genetics produces strong body relaxation and a noticeable euphoric mental effect.

Is Double OG indica or sativa? The cultivar is generally classified as an indica-dominant hybrid. While it delivers a mental uplift during the early stages of the high, the overall experience leans toward deep physical relaxation.

Why does Double OG smell like fuel and pine? The aroma comes primarily from its OG Kush heritage. Terpenes such as myrcene, limonene, and caryophyllene interact to produce the distinctive citrus, diesel, and pine notes associated with kush strains.

Is Double OG good for nighttime use? Many cannabis consumers prefer it in the evening. The relaxing body effects can become quite heavy as the high progresses, making it well suited for unwinding after a long day.

Is Double OG easy to grow? Growers with moderate experience generally manage it successfully. While the plant is fairly resilient, attention to humidity and airflow is important because the dense buds can trap moisture during flowering.
Final Thoughts on Double OG

Among the many cannabis varieties that trace their heritage to OG Kush, this cultivar stands out for embracing the lineage without dilution. By pairing two OG Kush parents, breeders created a marijuana strain that intensifies the aroma, potency, and resin production associated with one of the most influential cannabis genetics ever developed.

For cannabis enthusiasts who enjoy classic West Coast weed profiles, the plant delivers a familiar yet amplified experience. Pungent citrus-fuel aromas, frosty buds, and a deeply relaxing high combine into a cultivar that feels both traditional and powerful. Whether grown for its impressive trichome production or enjoyed for its calming effects, Double OG continues to appeal to those who appreciate the enduring legacy of OG Kush in modern cannabis culture .
